market_name: Putin out as President of Russia by December 31, 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the Polymarket move is corroborated by any credible newswire (Reuters/Bloomberg/TASS) on Putin's health or status; distinguish thin-book noise from a real signal.
time_plan.1h: Watch Brent/WTI futures and European TTF gas for a coordinated risk premium build; check ruble proxies if any trade.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether oil move is holding or fading and whether narrative is 'chaos' (bullish) vs 'de-escalation' (bearish).
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against official Kremlin statements; if debunked, expect mean reversion of any oil premium.
time_plan.12h: Mark final oil move, compare to safe-haven behavior, and log whether the prediction-market spike preceded any public confirmation.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of Putin leaving power would signal potential political instability in a major energy exporter. Instability/chaos scenarios typically inject a geopolitical supply-risk premium into oil (bullish), but a leadership change could equally be read as a path toward de-escalation of the Ukraine war and eventual sanctions relief (bearish). The net sign is genuinely ambiguous, so directional conviction is low; the tail is fat in both directions.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether the market move coincides with any credible reporting; check DXY and Treasury futures for corroborating risk-off.
time_plan.1h: Watch gold spot and VIX/equity index futures for a joint flight-to-safety pattern.
time_plan.2h: Determine if the safe-haven bid is broadening (JPY, CHF, USTs) or isolated noise.
time_plan.6h: Reassess against official denials/confirmations; fade the thesis if no corroboration emerges.
time_plan.12h: Record final gold move and whether the prediction-market signal led public news flow.

predictions.reasoning: Leadership uncertainty in a nuclear-armed state is a classic safe-haven catalyst. A credible spike in the probability of Putin's removal would likely trigger a modest risk-off bid into gold regardless of whether the ultimate outcome is escalation or de-escalation, because the transition itself raises tail risk. The expected magnitude is small unless the signal is confirmed by real reporting.

evidence_used: Market question implies probability of Putin ceasing to be Russian president by end-2026
Russia is a top-3 global oil/gas exporter; leadership instability affects energy risk premia
Nuclear-armed state leadership transitions are historical safe-haven catalysts
Russian domestic assets are largely uninvestable to Western capital due to sanctions, so direct proxies are weak
uncertainty_notes: Directional sign for oil is fundamentally ambiguous: chaos (bullish) vs de-escalation/sanctions relief (bearish)
Polymarket books on long-dated political survival markets are thin and prone to noise, not necessarily information leakage
Most Russia-direct instruments (RSX, ruble) are delisted/frozen, limiting clean proxies
A 12h window is short for a slow-moving political-survival question to produce large asset moves absent a concrete headline

llm_justification.summary: A sharp move in the probability that Putin leaves the Russian presidency would signal rising political-instability tail risk in a major energy exporter and nuclear power. The cleanest liquid implications are a geopolitical risk premium in oil (direction genuinely ambiguous—instability is bullish, de-escalation/sanctions-relief hopes are bearish) and a modest safe-haven bid into gold. Conviction and magnitudes are low because the mapping is weak, proxies are indirect, sanctions have severed direct Russia exposure, and thin prediction-market books generate noise. Neither prediction is expected to clear the 700bps tradable threshold absent confirmed public reporting.
key_assumptions: A meaningful probability spike, not just noise, is what triggers analysis
The move is at least partly information-driven rather than pure liquidity noise
Oil and gold remain the most liquid, accessible proxies for Russia political risk given sanctions
No confirmed public headline has already priced the event at signal time
failure_modes: The prediction-market move is thin-book noise with no informational content, so no asset moves
The event is already public/priced, making any subsequent asset move stale
Oil direction is wrong because the market reads a Putin exit as war de-escalation (bearish) rather than chaos (bullish)
Gold and oil are only weakly exposed to Russian political specifics on a 12h horizon; macro factors (Fed, DXY) dominate
Sanctions mean the most sensitive assets (ruble, Russian equities) cannot be traded, so the true signal has no liquid expression
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
